status.comment: Opt-in Rust methodology and runtime; installation never selects or starts a campaign.

p.SELECTION: ZAP is an opt-in adaptive campaign methodology and Rust runtime. Loading, installing, building or querying this package does not select it for a campaign, replace a multi-user-planning context, activate a charter, invoke a model, or authorize execution. A current coordinator remains authoritative until the Owner explicitly selects a supported migration and exact trust configuration.

p.SCOPED-READING: For campaign design use zap-draft and ZAP-METHODOLOGY.xml. For bounded store reads, preparation and reconciliation use zap-state. For explicitly configured execution, trusted control, native-driver coordination or backend serving use zap-run and ZAP-RUNTIME.xml. For strategic-map projections and descriptive work assessments read ZAP-STRATEGIC-MAP.xml and ZAP-STRATEGIC-MAP-GUIDE.md; select an exact strategy and preserve the separate runtime/admission boundary. Read ZAP-RUST-STORAGE.xml for persistence and recovery, ZAP-AGENT-PROTOCOL.xml for packet and driver behavior, and ZAP-LOWERING-AND-DREAMER.xml for lowering, offline bundles and detached exploration. Workers with explicit packets keep their packet scope; this flow does not make them central coordinators.

p.CAPABILITIES: The package declares the native Rust zap binary, typed application service, transactional store, automatic coordinator, authenticated loopback JSON and event-stream interface, native AgentHost bridge, read-only effect preparation, Dreamer projection, economics and Owner gates, filesystem material/workspace adapters, portable offline archives, legacy import and durable reconciliation. Capability output derives from actual registrations. The binary never launches a native harness by itself; a cooperating host performs the external launch and returns typed receipts. Installation and import remain inert, and the package contains no canvas or IDE client.

p.PORTABILITY: Normal package execution is Rust-only and requires no Python, GitHub account, external database service, VibeVM source checkout, or repository-specific path. Build requires an actual Vibe build/bin-capable executable, the Rust toolchain and locally available declared packages for offline use. Credentials, stores, service leases, packets, captures, workspaces, archives and logs remain user-local runtime material outside the installed source payload.
